prompt_subtasks.item: PASS 1 (Extraction): reconstruct (i) a USER-DRIVEN Feature Backlog, (ii) an AGENT-CENTRIC Specification Backlog (step-wise), plus Prompt Ledger + Replay Package + Repo Stats, and WRITE:
SPECIFICATION_BACKLOG.md
README.md (must reference SPECIFICATION_BACKLOG.md)
PASS 2 (Interpretation): characterize strategies, outcomes/quality, interaction demand; correlate with lightweight metrics.
I will NOT provide transcripts proactively.
You must analyze the repo as-is (git history may be minimal/absent).
Codex stores local state under CODEX_HOME (defaults to ~/.codex).
$CODEX_HOME/sessions/**.jsonl (session event streams)
$CODEX_HOME/history.jsonl (if history persistence is enabled)
other logs/caches under CODEX_HOME as available
Prefer session evidence from these artifacts; fall back to repo-only when unavailable.
Do NOT invent features, decisions, commands, or outcomes.
Every claim must be traceable to evidence from: repo files, git commits (if any), CODEX_HOME session artifacts, and run/test logs you executed.
If you infer anything, label it INFERRED and justify why.
Redact secrets (tokens/keys) if encountered in repo or logs.
Keep quotes short (<= 25 words). Prefer pointers.
[R:path:lines] repo file references (include line ranges when possible)
[G:commit <hash>] git commit references
[T:session <id/filename>:event_###] session-log references (or timestamp ranges)
[L:run_<n>] outputs of build/test/run commands you executed
[S:stats_run_<n>] outputs of repo statistics commands
Do NOT list them in the Feature Backlog.
If explicitly requested by the user for reproducibility, list them in a separate section:
Specification Backlog (agent-centric changes) and/or
PASS 2 as “Agent-Initiated / Internal Decisions”.
why it blocks the analysis,
what artifact would resolve it,
a “Default if unanswered” assumption.
repo root, primary language(s), entry points, build system, test framework, CI configs.
git metadata if present: branch, HEAD, remotes.
